text:
The fix is complete. Here's what changed in `textkit/slug.py`:

1. **`re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)`** — Added the `+` quantifier so that consecutive non-alphanumeric characters are collapsed into a single hyphen instead of producing multiple hyphens.
2. **`text.strip("-")`** — Removes any leading or trailing hyphens.

These two changes ensure `slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello-world"` (instead of `"hello--world-"`) and `slugify("--a--b--")` returns `"a-b"` (instead of `"-a-b-"`). All existing tests pass.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify to collapse consecutive non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen (using `+` quantifier in regex) and strip leading/trailing hyphens (using `strip("-")`). This resolves the double-hyphen and trailing-hyphen issues described in the issue.
